title: John Durretts Are Oldest Couple Residing At Savoy
text:
PIONEERS AT SAVOY—First couple at Savoy from the Standpoint of age and length of married life are Mr. and Mrs. John Durrett, who have been married 62 years and have resided in Savoy since 1889. (Herald photo.)

John Durretts Are Oldest Couple Residing At Savoy

Herald News Service)

SAVOY.—Mr. and Mrs. John Durrett have the honor of holding the first place in Savoy as to their age and the length of marriage.

Mrs. Durrett celebrated her 86th birthday April 3, and her 62nd wedding anniversay last Dec. 18. She is a native of Kentucky, and was born near Greensburg on April 3, 1861. The couple resided in Kentucky about five years before coming to Savoy to make their home. She was Miss Fannie Robinson before her marriage. She had two sisters, but no brothers. Her mother was Mrs. Mary Teresa Robinson, and made her home with the Durett family. She died in 1925 in Savoy at the age of 87.

Mr. Durrett will celebate 87th birthday Sept. 7. He als a native of Kentucky. He was born in 1860, near Campbellesville, Taylor[?] County, Kentucky. He came to Texas the first time with his brother, the late Jim Durrett, in 1881, making the trip in a wagon. The trip took 36 days. They encountered all the hardships of the pioneer travel.

His parents, the late Dr. and Mrs. Joel Durrett, joined them in Savoy later, bringing with them the family of two other brothers, the late Bill and the late Ed[?] Durrett, and five sisters, Mrs. Lily King of Dallas, Mrs. Sue Pedigo of Dallas, and Mrs. Pink Davis of Wichita Falls, and the late Mrs. Hattie Simmons and the late Mrs. Sally McQueen.

Dr. Durrett practiced medicine in Savoy and the surrounding communities until a short time before his death at the age of [illegible]. Mrs. Durrett died at the age of [illegible]. The couple lived to see all their children past middle-nine were living at the [illegible] their mother's death.

Mr. and Mrs. Durrett have their home in Savoy since[?] with the exception of two[?] they resided in Gunter. M[?] rett owned and operated [illegible] ton gin for several years [illegible] engaged in farming before [illegible]

The couple have two so[?] mie Durrett of Post, Te[?] Herbert Durrett of Sherm[?] two daughters, Mrs. Ella Hood of Fort Worth, and [illegible] esa Morgan of Savoy, th[?] daughters, Miss Maxine [illegible] of Post, Miss George An[?] of Savoy, and Mrs. Mar[?] Hood Berry of Fort W[?] one grandson, Thomas Mu[?] of Grand Prarie and t[?] grand children.
notes: Two portrait photographs at top: Mr. and Mrs. John Durrett. Caption reads 'PIONEERS AT SAVOY'. Right side of article is clipped/torn; several passages are partially illegible and have been marked accordingly. 'anniversay' is original spelling (not 'anniversary').
